name: CV / Resume Analysis - Blockchain Developer
description: Extraction rules and signal mappings for Blockchain Developer CVs/resumes. Blockchain development has unusually strong GitHub evidence — working code, deployed contract addresses, and verified contracts on Etherscan are primary sources. CV corroborates GitHub signals and provides deployment scale, team context, and business impact. NOTE: Specific maps_to composite keys are stored within individual skill files under evidence.cv.

quality_indicators: Named protocols with deployed contract addresses or Etherscan links
TVL figures (e.g., 'secured $5M TVL in first month') or transaction volume metrics
Specific vulnerability mitigations implemented (e.g., 'resolved reentrancy identified in audit')
Named security tools used in professional context (Slither, Echidna, MythX, OpenZeppelin Defender)
Multi-chain deployment experience with specific chain names
Quantified test coverage metrics (e.g., '98% line coverage, 500+ fuzz test iterations')
Audit firm names if contracts were professionally audited (Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, ConsenSys Diligence)
GitHub repository link with meaningful commit history
Mainnet or testnet contract addresses for verification
Described architectural decisions (why specific proxy pattern was chosen, why Foundry over Hardhat)
DeFi TVL, NFT mint volume, DAO proposal count, or other on-chain impact metrics

skills_list.notes: Listing 'Solidity' without project context provides low signal. Framework names (Hardhat, Foundry) without test counts or deployment history are low strength. Security tool names (Slither, Echidna) with no evidence of use are weak.

recognized_certifications: Certified Blockchain Developer (CBD) — Blockchain Training Alliance
Ethereum Developer Certification — Ethereum Foundation / ConsenSys Academy

patterns.pattern: Developed and deployed Solidity smart contracts on Ethereum mainnet or EVM-compatible chains
Wrote unit tests, integration tests, or property-based fuzz tests for smart contracts
Implemented ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, or ERC-4626 token standards
Used Hardhat, Foundry, Truffle, or Brownie as development framework
Integrated Chainlink Data Feeds, VRF, Automation, or CCIP
Conducted security analysis using Slither, Echidna, MythX, or Manticore
Implemented upgradeable proxy patterns (UUPS, Transparent, Beacon, Diamond)
Deployed on L2 networks (Arbitrum, Optimism, zkSync, StarkNet, Base, Polygon zkEVM)
Built DeFi protocols, AMM integrations, lending systems, or yield vaults
Developed Solana programs with Anchor framework or Substrate pallets in Rust
Built DAO governance contracts or implemented on-chain voting systems
Set up smart contract monitoring with The Graph, Tenderly, or OpenZeppelin Defender

important_notes: Etherscan-verified mainnet contract addresses mentioned in CV are the strongest CV evidence — they are independently verifiable
TVL and on-chain transaction volume are the blockchain equivalent of production traffic metrics — weight them highly
Security audit participation (as developer preparing for audit, or as reviewer) is a strong senior signal
Rust proficiency for Solana or Substrate development is significantly rarer and higher value than Solidity alone
Participation in on-chain governance, hackathon wins, or bug bounty payouts are high-signal credibility indicators
CTF (Capture the Flag) competition wins or Ethernaut/Damn Vulnerable DeFi completion indicate security depth
